purpose: Test whether multiple routed user-interest vectors repair the V2 retrieval bottleneck without reopening the closed attention/pooling family or relying on unobserved ranking labels.
hypothesis: A K=2 dynamic-routing interest representation can improve V2 Validation retrieval because one normalized user vector may compress distinct recent history interests.
single_core_variable: user_encoder=dynamic_routing_multi_interest with K=2 and routing_iterations=3; item tower, History-10 Train/Validation artifact, full-catalog softmax, scaled-cosine contract and optimizer remain fixed.
acceptance_rule: Against the frozen V2 aligned baseline, require overall Recall@10 improvement of at least 0.003, NDCG@10 improvement of at least 0.002, AQ3 Recall@10 and Tail PQ0 Recall@10 each non-inferior within 0.002, and AQ0-AQ3 Recall@10 gap no worse by more than 0.002. No post-result threshold, K, routing-iteration, or seed changes.
closure: This is a new retrieval hypothesis family with at most two formal candidates. If K=2 fails, diagnose its fixed Validation evidence before proposing at most one non-equivalent candidate; otherwise close the family.
